string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing serves as the national capital of China and a direct-administered municipality. It is the political and cultural hub of the nation with more than three thousand years of history. Well-known landmarks include the Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square and nearby sections of the Great Wall. National government offices, top museums and leading universities are located within this city.

Shanghai is the largest city of China and a key international financial centre on the Yangtze River delta. It is one of four direct-administered municipalities. The city combines classic historical architecture and modern high-rise buildings. Its large ports support domestic and overseas trade and attract many visitors and business people every year.

Chongqing is a big inland direct-administered municipality in the southwest area of China. It lies at the meeting point of Yangtze River and Jialing River and is widely known as the mountain city. It has a solid industrial foundation and booming local economy. Unique hillside landscapes and famous local food draw large numbers of tourists.

Tianjin is a direct-administered municipality next to Beijing. It keeps many historic buildings mixing Chinese style and western design from earlier international settlements. It works as an important northern port and industrial base. It has special local food culture and convenient transport connections with the capital.
